ASEAN partners gather at the opening of the International Media Center and Partners Pavilion, featuring GCash-powered Cebuano micro-entrepreneurs during the largest leadership gathering in Cebu

The superapp will be bringing cashless convenience, financial inclusion to the heart of the region’s largest leadership gathering

Editor’s note: This press release is sponsored by GCash and was handled by BrandRap, the sales and marketing arm of Rappler. No member of the news and editorial team participated in the publishing of this piece.

GCash, one of the Philippines’ leading financial technology platforms, is proud to support the 48th ASEAN Summit as an official partner to bring cashless convenience and financial inclusion at the region’s largest leadership gathering.

The 48th ASEAN Summit in Lapu-Lapu City, Cebu is one of the highest-level meetings of the regional bloc for the year, where heads of state from 11 member countries come together to discuss and decide on key regional issues.

“We are incredibly honored to be a huge part of the Philippines’ ASEAN Chairship. Our partnership with ASEAN provides us a chance to showcase Filipino innovation on the global stage and demonstrate how the Philippines is leading the charge toward a more integrated, digital ASEAN region,” GCash general manager for GCash for Business Paul Albano said.

EMPOWERING CEBUANO MSMEs. GCash-powered micro-entrepreneurs from Cebu showcases local products at the ASEAN’s Partners Pavillion.



At the Partners Pavillion, GCash is powering booths featuring Cebuano micro-entrepreneurs who are engaged in home décor, pastries and confections, handcrafted woven goods, chocolates, dairy and food items, and locally made souvenirs and artisan crafts. These include Adorno ’72 Home Decors, Audrey’s Confectioneries, Dahlia Chocolates, Hinablon sa Cebu, Holicow, Island Souvenirs, Profoods, Rambie’s Collection, Tuburan, and Ver & Ver Handicrafts.

“By supporting the MSME marketplace at the pavilion and enabling cashless transactions for Cebuano micro-entrepreneurs, we are showing how digital financial inclusion creates tangible, real-world impact,” Albano added.

The booth, in addition, will feature on-site card printing and dedicated customer experience representatives to assist users and address inquiries in real time.

It will also highlight a range of GCash offerings, including lending and wealth management products, GCash for Business payment solutions and devices, as well as services tailored for overseas Filipinos.

Beyond product demonstrations, the booth aims to boost MSME digitalization by onboarding new merchants to GCash for Business and showcasing how digital tools can help local enterprises grow and scale in an increasingly cashless economy.

“We are powering the MSME marketplace by bringing cashless payments to Cebuano micro-entrepreneurs. When a local vendor can accept a digital payment as easily as a major retailer, that is digital financial inclusion in practice,” Albano added.

GCash will also join key side events at the summit to participate in discussions on digital transformation and advance wider access to financial services across the region.

The summit, with the theme “Navigating Our Future, Together” is being held this week in Lapu-Lapu City, Cebu, Philippines, as part of the country’s ASEAN chairmanship.

The event gathers leaders from all 11 ASEAN member states, along with thousands of delegates, officials, and international media.

Discussions will center on energy security, food security, regional stability, and protection of ASEAN citizens, alongside broader themes of economic integration, sustainability, and digital cooperation.For more information on ASEAN, visit https://asean2026.gov.ph. – Rappler.com

World.title: Influencers, digital experts gather at WPP Media’s Creatorverse
World.content:
This is AI generated summarization, which may have errors. For context, always refer to the full article.

Brands, creators, media, and experts were present the content creation conference, in pursuit of shaping the future of influence

Editor’s note: This press release was submitted by WPP Media Philippines and was handled by BrandRap, the sales and marketing arm of Rappler. No member of the news and editorial team participated in the publishing of this piece.

WPP Media hosted Creatorverse: Beyond the Algorithm in Manila — its inaugural and landmark gathering for content creators in the Philippines — bringing together the country’s leading brands, creators, media publishers, and experts to tackle the creator economy not just as a channel but as a discipline.

The Philippines is not a market where brands are still debating whether social media and creators matter. Filipinos are among the world’s most active social media users, spending more time online than almost any other nationality — and they are profoundly shaped by the voices, communities, and content they encounter. The question for Philippine brands has never been if the creator economy is relevant, but it has always been how to do it properly, and Creatorverse was brought forth to answer that question.

A roster of distinguished experts shared critical insights throughout the event. They covered foundational aspects of the creator economy, the evolving role of media publishers, strategies for leveraging regional and local market advantages, and innovative approaches to branded content creation. The speakers also delved into the transformative power of AI in personalizing creative delivery and optimizing influence strategies for the future of marketing.

“No single brand, agency, or creator builds the future of this industry alone. What we need, and what today was about, is the whole ecosystem in the same room, speaking the same language,” Crisela Cervantes, CEO of WPP Media Philippines said.

The event featured panel discussions that thoroughly explored current dynamics and future opportunities within the evolving creator landscape. Critical dialogues centered on sophisticated monetization strategies, including how creators could effectively turn their content into direct revenue.

Experts also discussed the vital role of engaging audiences through interactive and playful content, as well as the pervasive impact of artificial intelligence in enhancing creative processes and broadening reach. These engaging conversations were significantly enriched by the participation of prominent Key Opinion Leaders (KOLs) who offered practical experiences and forward-looking perspectives.

The impactful sessions featured contributions from the following notable speakers and panelists: Malyn Molina of ASEAN Business Advisory Council, Howard Go of Summit Media, Bryan Yap of Republiq Group of Companies, Sanjay Vasudeva of Buzzone, Emir Caglayan of WPP Media Singapore, Geia Lopez of Google Southeast Asia, Erwann Heussaff of The Fat Kid Inside Studios and FEATR Media, and content creators Abi Marquez, Myrtle Sarrosa, Teree Daisuke, Nicole Hyala, and Mike Phillips.

More than a demonstration of capabilities, the event served as an open forum, a space where brands already navigating the creator economy shared what’s working, where the gaps remain, and what a more mature, more accountable industry could look like for everyone. In a market as culturally rich and digitally active as the Philippines — where regional communities, platform behaviour, and creator relationships vary enormously — that kind of honest, cross-industry dialogue is rare and necessary.

“Filipino creators don’t just have audiences, they have communities. That is a fundamentally different kind of relationship, and the whole industry benefits when we build around that truth,” Said KB Ignacio, senior director of WPP Media Philippines.

Creatorverse: Beyond the Algorithm powerfully reaffirmed WPP Media’s commitment to shaping, conquering, and helping brands become part of the dynamic creator universe. The event showcased how WPP’s unique blend of scale, integrated strategy, and AI-powered creativity can create lasting impact for brands, creators and consumers. – Rappler.com

World.title: NBI to appeal for law to regulate socmed, separate ‘fake’ journalists
World.content:
Social media personality and Peanut Gallery Media Network (PGMN) founder Franco Mabanta and four others are in the custody of the National Bureau of Investigation after being arrested for the alleged extortion of former Speaker Martin Romualdez. (Photo: Mary Joy Salcedo/INQUIRER)

MANILA, Philippines — The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) will appeal for Congress to pass a law that would regulate social media and separate real journalists from the “fakes” posing to be legit.

NBI Director Mevin Matibag said this in an ambush interview on Thursday after social media personality Franco Mabanta, founder of online channel Peanut Gallery Media Network (PGMN), asserted that his arrest over an “extortion” case against former House Speaker Martin Romualdez is an issue of “press freedom.”

‘WE’RE INNOCENT’WATCH: Social media personality and Peanut Gallery Media Network (PGMN) founder Franco Mabanta denies trying to extort P350 million from former Speaker Martin Romualdez. pic.twitter.com/qtiVrbxvWp — MJ Salcedo (@MJSalcedoINQ) May 6, 2026

Mabanta, along with four others, was nabbed by the NBI in Pasig City on Tuesday evening after Romualdez’s camp filed a complaint that the PGMN founder tried to extort up to P350 million from him in exchange for not releasing an alleged “exposé video” that would supposedly link him to corruption in the House of Representatives.

Article continues after this 

READ: NBI nabs PGMN founder Franco Mabanta for alleged extortion vs Romualdez

“Setting aside all the noise and all the political issues that are being talked about, the lesson we have here is that we should crack down on social media that is posing as a news outfit,” Matibag said.

“So probably we will push legislation to that effect to regulate, not to curtail, but to regulate or to give some rules and regulations on what the behavior is. Because there are so many people today who don’t have a journalism background, who don’t study journalism, who are mass media,” he pointed out.

Matibag said the NBI will immediately push the appeal to Congress, emphasizing that he has already instructed the bureau’s staff to prepare a draft bill and is also talking with other lawmakers about it.

READ: NBI: PGMN’s CJ Hirro person of interest in Romualdez ‘extortion’ case

Article continues after this 

Matibag then questioned the supposed “exposé video” of the PGMN against Romualdez, saying that their intention for this is only to “get a big payout.”

“Why is that video, it was made last year, why isn’t it coming out? I mean, there is no intention of putting out this video. The intention is to get a big payout. Big profit. Which is P350 million ang original, down to P300 million. So looking back at history, they’re trying to build up,” he said, referring to the supposed amount that Mabanta tried to extort from Romualdez.

Article continues after this 

“They said they did a long research. Of course, it seems like you’re producing a blockbuster film that also requires a blockbuster profit,” he argued.

The NBI director said they are also looking into the supposed 90-minute expose video that Mabanta recently mentioned in his statement.

Mabanta said in a statement on Wednesday that over the last five months, the PGMN “completed immense, comprehensive, painful research” about the Romualdez’s supposed corruption while he was still speaker of the House of Representatives.

“What we have is devastating. The episode was filmed several weeks ago. It has been fully edited — it is 90 minutes-long, packed with hard evidence, and ready for release,” the PGMN founder said.

Meanwhile, in a statement on Thursday, Romualdez’s camp argued that the PGMN was not engaged in journalism and “is twisting the narrative,” pointed out that the congressman only filed the complaint before the NBI since he was threatened with payment in exchange for silence.

‘Mabanta, others at the NBI detention center’

Following their arrest on Tuesday evening, Mabanta and four others have been detained at the NBI detention facility in Muntinlupa City since 6 p.m. on Thursday.

Matibag said they are waiting for the resolution from the Pasig City Regional Trial Court, adding that there will be a recommended bail for their case.

“If they will post bail, we are obligated to release Franco Mabanta and all the others, provided there are no other cases pending in any court,” he said.

The bail amount has not yet been disclosed, as of this writing.

World.title: Mollenido slay: Cop’s husband cleared in obstruction of justice rap
World.content:
LAID TO REST. A memorial service is held for Police Senior Master Sgt. Diane Marie Mollenido and her son, John Ysmael, before their cremated remains are buried at Heritage Memorial Park in Taguig City on February 5, 2026. — CONTRIBUTED PHOTO

MANILA, Philippines — Dismissed Police Master Sgt. John Mollenido was cleared of an obstruction of justice case in connection with the killing of his wife, Police Senior Master Sgt. Diane Mollenido, and his son, John Ysmael.

“After a thorough evaluation of the evidence on record, the [Malolos] Office of the City Prosecutor found no prima facie evidence with reasonable certainty of conviction to justify the filing of charges in court,” John’s lawyer, Cristobal Rimando, said in a statement on Thursday.

“The Prosecutor expressly recognized significant procedural lapses in the handling of the alleged evidence, including the failure of concerned authorities to properly inventory, document, and turn over the personal effects of the deceased,” he added.

Article continues after this 

READ: Napolcom sacks slain cop’s husband for grave misconduct, obstruction

John was charged with obstruction of justice by police investigators for supposedly insisting on cremating Diane’s remains despite an ongoing investigation, police previously said.

Rimando previously alleged that police investigators had released custody of Diane’s remains to John, giving him authority to have them cremated.

“This ruling affirms what we have consistently maintained from the very beginning: that our client acted in good faith, without malicious intent, and under extraordinary circumstances,” Rimando said in a statement.

John was dismissed from the police service by the National Police Commission (Napolcom) last Saturday in connection with the obstruction case.

Article continues after this 

“While certain public narratives sought to prematurely assign criminal liability, this resolution serves as a reminder that truth must be determined through proper legal processes—not speculation or public pressure,” Rimando said.

“Our client remains committed to cooperating with all lawful proceedings involving other matters and will continue to avail of every legal remedy necessary to protect his rights, reputation, and interests,” it added.

Article continues after this 

The Inquirer sought comment from Napolcom Commissioner Rafael Calinisan on whether the dismissal of the criminal obstruction charge would affect the already-decided administrative case against John, but he has yet to respond.

Diane and John Ysmael were allegedly killed by her niece and car agent Pia Katrina Panganiban; Pia’s husband, Christian Suarez; and Pia’s helper, Gil Dy Jr., in Quezon City last January.

World.title: Luistro trusts Senate to convene impeach court if Duterte case is sent
World.content:
House justice committee chair and Batangas Rep. Gerville Luistro presides over a hearing on the Duterte impeachment on Monday, May 4, 2026. — Screengrab from House of Representatives/Facebook

MANILA, Philippines — Batangas Rep. Gerville Luistro believes the Senate will convene an impeachment court once the articles of impeachment against Vice President Sara Duterte are approved, noting there is no reason for the chamber not to proceed with a trial.

In an interview on Thursday, Luistro said the only way for the Senate to refrain from proceeding with a trial is if the Supreme Court (SC) issues a temporary restraining order (TRO).

“We’ve heard it from some of the senators from the Duterte bloc that they will be opposing the impeachment complaint … But of course, we are positive and hopeful considering that we follow the Constitution, the Supreme Court decision, and the rules of impeachment proceedings,” she added.

Article continues after this 

Luistro, chairperson of the House of Representatives’ committee on justice, said there is no reason to delay the trial because they have complied with the 1987 Constitution and the Supreme Court decision on the first set of impeachment complaints.

“We’re positive and hopeful that there are no grounds why they should stop the Senate from convening an impeachment court. I don’t see any reason why the Senate should stop from convening into an impeachment court,” she said.

“Up to now, no TRO has been issued by the Supreme Court, which means that no law was violated, no rule was violated by the House of Representatives insofar as initiating the impeachment complaints is concerned,” she added.

The justice panel approved the committee report containing the articles of impeachment against Duterte last Monday, May 4.

On May 5, the committee report was brought to the House plenary, and on Wednesday, electronic copies were distributed to lawmakers.

Article continues after this 

After the justice panel’s approval of the committee report—and amid talks that the House has already secured enough votes to impeach Duterte—Senate President Vicente “Tito” Sotto III said the impeachment court will convene as soon as the chamber receives the articles of impeachment, “no matter what others say.”

READ: Sotto: Impeach court automatically convenes once Duterte case received

Article continues after this 

Sotto made the statement after Sen. Robinhood Padilla said it is the minority’s “job to oppose” everything in the Senate, including the impeachment of Duterte.

“Based on the Constitution, it’s automatic. That’s our job. No matter what others say, what matters is what the Constitution says: when the Articles of Impeachment are received, we convene as an impeachment court,” Sotto said in Filipino.

READ: Senate minority airs views on possible Sara Duterte impeachment trial

Committee Report (CR) No. 261, which contains the articles of impeachment, consolidated the grounds into four from the seven grounds in the third impeachment complaint and the six in the fourth impeachment complaint.

READ: Articles of impeachment vs Sara Duterte reach House plenary

According to CR No. 261, the grounds from the two complaints were consolidated into four:

• Culpable violation of the Constitution, graft and corruption, and betrayal of public trust through the systematic liquidation, misuse, misappropriation, and irregular use of confidential funds amounting to P500 million under the Office of the Vice President and P112.5 million under the Department of Education (DepEd)

• Culpable violation of the Constitution and betrayal of public trust when Duterte allegedly amassed unexplained wealth manifestly disproportionate to her lawful income and earnings during her incumbency as a public official

• Bribery, graft and corruption, culpable violation of the Constitution, and betrayal of public trust when she allegedly gave monetary gifts or payments to DepEd officials to induce the violation and circumvention of procurement and other related laws

• Culpable violation of the Constitution, high crimes, and betrayal of public trust for allegedly contracting the assassination of the president, the first lady, and the former speaker of the House, making grave threats, and actively inciting sedition against the Republic

READ: Secret funds, unexplained wealth: Duterte impeach articles cut to 4 grounds

Several sources privy to conversations within the House believe the chamber can come near or match the 215 signatures that backed the first impeachment bid against Duterte in 2025, as many lawmakers have already signified their support.

READ: 215 lawmakers back 2026 Duterte impeachment, matching 2025 tally – Ridon

One insider close to lawmakers said there may still be considerable work needed to secure 200 affirmative votes, but it is possible.

Another source said they have already secured 200 signatures.

World.title: Duterte impeachment: QC court junks Carpio bid vs House subpoena on ITRs
World.content:
Vice President Sara Duterte and lawyer Manases Carpio

MANILA, Philippines — The Quezon City Regional Trial Court has dismissed the petition filed by Atty. Manases Carpio, husband of Vice President Sara Duterte, seeking to block the House of Representatives justice panel from issuing a subpoena for the couple’s annual income tax returns as part of the impeachment proceedings against his wife.

In a five-page ruling, Quezon City RTC Branch 81 Presiding Judge Madonna Echiverri said the court cannot grant the injunctive relief sought by Carpio, as doing so would interfere with the House’s constitutional impeachment powers.

“On the matter of the issuance of a writ of preliminary injunction, it has been settled that the injunction is directed only to the party litigants, without in any manner interfering with the court,” the court said.

Article continues after this 

The petitioners sought to stop respondents, who were acting in their official capacity as a committee of the House of Representatives, where the impeachment complaints were filed.

READ: 215 lawmakers back 2026 Duterte impeachment, matching 2025 tally – Ridon

The court said judicial review over a constitutional organ like the House committee on justice (HCOJ) properly belongs to the Supreme Court.

“The respondents are acting in their official capacity as part of the HCOJ, a co-equal branch of government; hence, the case at bench should have been filed with the Supreme Court,” the court said.

The respondents in the case are Speaker Faustino “Bojie” Dy, justice panel chairperson Batangas Rep. Jinky Luistro, and Bureau of Internal Revenue Commissioner Charlito Mendoza.

Article continues after this 

The court said the House holds the “exclusive power to initiate all cases of impeachment” under the 1987 Constitution. Consequently, a writ of prohibition cannot be issued against a validly constituted body exercising its legal mandate.

It added that the subpoenas issued by the respondents were done in the “valid exercise of said inherent powers.”

Article continues after this 

On the submitted news articles and YouTube links of the proceedings presented as evidence by the Carpio camp, the court said: “YouTube links cannot be the subject of a mandatory judicial notice.”

The lower court added that newspapers cannot also be the subject of discretionary judicial notice.

“Newspaper articles amount to ‘hearsay evidence, twice removed’ and are therefore not only inadmissible but without probative value at all, whether objected to or not, unless offered for a purpose other than proving the truth of the matter asserted,” the court said.

The impeachment complaint against Duterte was unanimously approved last May 4, finding probable cause.

The charges against Duterte include alleged misuse of confidential funds, non-declaration of assets and unexplained wealth, and abuse of power and bribery.

World.title: Ridon: QC court ruling clears way for House impeachment vote vs Duterte
World.content:
Rep. Terry Ridon file photo. INQUIRER PHOTO / GRIG C. MONTEGRANDE

MANILA, Philippines — House Committee on Public Accounts Chair Terry Ridon on Thursday welcomed the dismissal of lawyer Manases “Mans” Carpio’s petition seeking to stop the impeachment proceedings against Vice President Sara Duterte, saying the ruling removes what he described as an unnecessary obstacle ahead of a crucial plenary vote on Monday.

“It is only right that the QC RTC dismissed Mans Carpio’s case. The petition had no legal basis and merely served as a disruption to the broader process of holding the Vice President accountable,” said Ridon, who also sits on the House Committee on Justice.

Ridon said income tax returns (ITRs) and related tax records may be treated as public documents when examined in constitutional proceedings such as impeachment cases.

Article continues after this 

READ: Lawmakers dismiss Carpio complaint, cite impeachment exemption

“ITRs and other tax documents are public documents and are not covered by confidentiality or privacy protections when they are part of constitutional and investigative proceedings like impeachment,” he said.

“With the dismissal of this case, the focus should now shift to the impeachment vote on Monday,” he added.

The remarks came after Quezon City Regional Trial Court Branch 81 junked Carpio’s petition seeking to halt the impeachment proceedings against Duterte, ruling that the judiciary cannot interfere with the House of Representatives’ constitutional authority over impeachment.

In a five-page order dated May 6, 2026, Presiding Judge Madonna C. Echiverri dismissed Carpio’s petition for prohibition and denied his request for a writ of preliminary injunction for lack of jurisdiction.

Article continues after this 

“The petition for prohibition is DISMISSED for lack of jurisdiction. The prayer for issuance of a writ of preliminary injunction is DENIED,” the court said.

READ: Carpio camp to media: Citing AMLC report against the law

Article continues after this 

Carpio sought to stop the House Committee on Justice from enforcing subpoenas and pursuing actions tied to the impeachment complaints against Duterte, particularly after the panel sought tax records and related documents allegedly linked to the vice president and her husband.

But the court ruled that the House panel was acting within powers granted by the Constitution and could not be restrained through prohibition or injunction.

“Respondents do not usurp but are in fact, as members of HCOJ are, by law, constituted to determine the sufficiency of the impeachment complaint against the Vice-President and eventually the determination of probable cause for the filing of the case to the Senate,” the order stated.

Citing Article XI of the 1987 Constitution, the RTC underscored that the House has the “exclusive power to initiate all cases of impeachment.”

The court also upheld the subpoena powers of the House justice panel, saying compulsory processes are inherent in carrying out impeachment proceedings effectively.

“Thus, the issuance of the subpoena duces tecum ad testificandum is an inherent power of the Committee, which is validly created by law, to carry out this constitutional mandate effectively in the conduct of its hearing,” the ruling stated.

The RTC likewise rejected Carpio’s argument that the House panel had no authority over him or documents allegedly linked to him and the vice president.

“Prohibition issues only against usurpers or those who exercise power which have not been vested by law,” the court said.

The court further ruled that injunctions cannot be used to block the House panel from performing its constitutional duties.

“To enjoin the public individuals in the performance of their duty in the determination of the sufficiency of the impeachment complaint is to prevent said body to exercise its quasi-judicial or ministerial functions,” the order stated.

The RTC also denied Carpio’s motion asking the court to take judicial notice of news reports and YouTube videos related to the House hearings, saying newspaper articles are “hearsay evidence, twice removed.”

The court said the petition should have been filed before the Supreme Court because the respondents were acting as part of a co-equal branch of government.

“In the case at bench, the respondents are acting in the official capacity as part of the HCOJ, a co-equal branch of the government hence, the case at bench should have been filed with the Supreme Court,” the order read.

World.title: Legit vape sellers call for tougher action vs illegal trade
World.content:
Philippine e-Cigarettes Industry Association.

MANILA, Philippines — The country’s vape industry on Thursday backed tougher enforcement against illegal vape traders, even as it urged lawmakers not to saddle legitimate businesses with penalties meant for black-market operators.

At a Senate hearing on the Vape Law, Philippine E-Cigarette Industry Association (PECIA) president Joey Dulay said the problem is not the absence of regulation but the weak implementation of existing rules.

“The market is flooded with unregistered, non-compliant illegal vape products,” Dulay told senators. “The real gap is not in the current law but in its enforcement, particularly against illicit products and black-market retailers.”

Article continues after this 

READ: DTI intensifies campaignvs illicit vape products

The hearing, led by Sen. Risa Hontiveros through the Senate committees on health and trade, focused heavily on growing concerns over youth access to vape products.

Hontiveros stressed that the review of the law was not intended to target the industry itself.

“This is not anti-industry. This is pro-health, pro-youth,” she said. “This is not about product but about people.”

Dulay said Republic Act No. 11900 already contains safeguards, including age restrictions, product standards and penalties for violators. What authorities need, he said, is stricter enforcement against sellers operating outside the law.

Article continues after this 

He drew a distinction between registered businesses and underground traders.

“There are two types of sellers in the market — a compliant industry and an illicit one,” he said. “Treating all vape sellers as if they are the same is not appropriate.”

Article continues after this 

READ: Vape waste: the harm that lingers

According to Dulay, illegal traders continue to ignore regulations regardless of proposed restrictions.

“They do not care whether the minimum age is set at 25, 28 or 31,” he said. “If flavors are restricted, they ignore that as well.”

Because they operate underground, he added, these sellers evade taxes, skip registration requirements and freely circulate products that often end up in the hands of minors.

PECIA, which represents more than 300 companies, appealed for what it described as a balanced approach — one that protects young people without crippling legitimate businesses that support thousands of jobs.

“We support efforts to prevent youth uptake, but we also need government support for adult smokers like us,” Dulay said.

He added that stronger enforcement against illegal supply chains would offer better protection than repeatedly reopening the law.

“The strongest protection for youth comes from strong enforcement of balanced regulation that removes illegal supply,” he said.

Dulay also said the group was willing to work with authorities in identifying violators.

“If you report retailers selling to minors or offering unlicensed products, we will work with the DTI and law enforcement agencies to go after these violators,” he said.

Representatives from major e-commerce platforms also appeared before the Senate panel and vowed closer coordination with regulators.

Speaking for Shopee Philippines, lawyer Jaimmie Hans-Segovia said online platforms continue to face attempts by bad actors to bypass safeguards through disguised listings and misleading product descriptions.

“We believe that enforcement is most effective when platforms and regulators operate from shared specific reference points,” she said.

Lazada Philippines representative John Kenneth Estiller likewise acknowledged that e-commerce platforms can be exploited, but said responsible operators should be part of the solution.

World.title: Over 1,100 SHS graduates hired on the spot during Labor Day job fairs
World.content:
Education Secretary Sonny Angara emphasized that providing immediate employment is a key strategy in breaking the cycle of poverty.

MANILA, Philippines — Reinforcing the promise of the K to 12 Program as a direct bridge to employment, at least 1,148 Senior High School (SHS) graduates were hired on the spot during Labor Day Job Fairs held nationwide.

The milestone underscores the growing confidence of employers in the preparedness and employability of SHS graduates. Of the roughly 11,000 graduates who joined the job fairs, many walked away with opportunities that offer not only immediate income but also a chance to help ease the financial burdens carried by their families.

“In line with President Bongbong Marcos’ vision of strengthening the education sector, the success of our SHS graduates proves that we are on the right path toward a brighter future for Filipino youth,” Education Secretary Sonny Angara said.

Article continues after this 

READ: DepEd expands summer remediation for struggling learners

Angara stressed that creating direct employment opportunities for graduates remains a crucial step in breaking the cycle of poverty.

“Our goal is to further expand these opportunities so that every Senior High School graduate is equipped with the skills and confidence needed to secure decent employment,” he added.

A key feature of this year’s Labor Day Job Fairs was the establishment of dedicated Green Lanes by the Department of Education (DepEd) and the Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE). The express lanes allowed SHS graduates to skip long queues by simply presenting a School ID or Certificate of Completion, streamlining the application process for first-time job seekers.

For Angel Balacayo, a graduate of Pacific Southbay College Inc. in General Santos City, the initiative opened the door to a long-awaited opportunity. Balacayo joined the Region 12 job fair in Koronadal City, hoping to find work and save for college after financial difficulties forced her to put higher education plans on hold.

Article continues after this 

Now employed at KCC Mall of Gensan, Balacayo said the priority lane made her first job application experience smoother and faster.

“The priority lane during the Job Fair was a huge help for Senior High School graduates like me because it sped up the entire job application process,” she said.

Article continues after this 

The initiative builds on the momentum of the Bagong Pilipinas Serbisyo Fair (BPSF) conducted in March, where more than 1,400 SHS and Alternative Learning System (ALS) graduates were likewise hired on the spot through one-stop service hubs.

In the same fairs, around 5,900 graduates also received free pre-employment requirements such as NBI and police clearances under the First Time Jobseekers Assistance Act (Republic Act No. 11261).

During his time in the Senate, Angara was the principal author of the law, which institutionalized government support for first-time job seekers by waiving fees for essential government-issued documents.
